title: Force display resolution via kernel video parameter
summary: If your monitor's native resolution is not detected correctly, you can force a specific resolution using the 'video=' kernel parameter. This is useful for Wayland compositors or when EDID data is faulty.
prerequisites: Know your desired resolution and refresh rate
Know your connector name (e.g., HDMI-A-1, DVI-I-1)

steps.explain: Find your connector name by running this command in the terminal:
steps.cmd: for p in /sys/class/drm/*/status; do con=${p%/status}; echo -n "${con#*/card?-}: "; cat $p; done
steps.expect: Output showing connector names and their status (connected/disconnected), e.g., 'HDMI-A-1: connected'.

steps.explain: Add the 'video=' parameter to your kernel command line in the bootloader configuration. Replace <CONNECTOR> with your connector name (e.g., HDMI-A-1), <XRES> with horizontal pixels, <YRES> with vertical pixels, and <REFRESH> with Hz.

placeholders.name: CONNECTOR
placeholders.description: The DRM connector name, e.g., HDMI-A-1, DVI-I-1
placeholders.discover_cmd: for p in /sys/class/drm/*/status; do con=${p%/status}; echo -n "${con#*/card?-}: "; cat $p; done

steps.explain: Regenerate your bootloader configuration to apply the changes. The exact command depends on your bootloader.

rollback.explain: Remove the 'video=' parameter from your bootloader configuration and regenerate the config.

warnings: Incorrect resolution settings can result in a black screen or no signal.
This method is primarily for the console and Wayland; Xorg may ignore it.
